title: Restore Our Fortunes, O Lord

questions.question: When the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:1 (ESV): "When the Lord restored the fortunes of Zion, we were like those who dream."

questions.question: Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with shouts of what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:2 (ESV): "Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with shouts of joy;"

questions.question: Then they said among the nations, "The Lord has done great things for whom?"
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:2 (ESV): "...The Lord has done great things for them."

questions.question: The Lord has done great things for us; we are what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:3 (ESV): "The Lord has done great things for us; we are glad."

questions.question: Restore our fortunes, O Lord, like streams in the what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:4 (ESV): "Restore our fortunes, O Lord, like streams in the Negeb!"

questions.question: Those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:5 (ESV): "Those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of joy!"

questions.question: He who goes out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, bringing his what?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:6 (ESV): "...shall come home with shouts of joy, bringing his sheaves with him."

questions.question: This Psalm is a Song of what?
What is the Negeb?
options: A desert region in the south
questions.correctAnswer: A desert region in the south

questions.question: What happens to the streams in the Negeb?
questions.explanation: The imagery is of sudden, refreshing restoration like flash floods in a dry wadi.

questions.question: Who said "The Lord has done great things for them"?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:2 (ESV): "Then they said among the nations..."

questions.question: What emotion accompanies sowing in verse 5?
What accompanies reaping in verse 5?
questions.explanation: Psalm 126:5 (ESV): "...shall reap with shouts of joy!"

questions.question: What does the sower bear as he goes out weeping?
What does the general theme of this Psalm reflect?
questions.explanation: The context of restoring fortunes (or turning captivity) points to the return from exile.

key_verse_text: Those who sow in tears shall reap with shouts of joy! He who goes out weeping, bearing the seed for sowing, shall come home with shouts of joy, bringing his sheaves with him.
